name: Lucena position (rook and pawn versus rook, pawn on the seventh)

plans.label: Build the bridge
plans.description: Walk the rook to the fourth rank first, then step the king out of the promotion square diagonally; when the checks come, block them by lowering the rook in front of the king — the bridge that escorts the pawn home.

success.note: The signature sees only that a white queen now exists; it cannot see that the bridge produced the promotion.

plans.label: Run the checking rook out of distance
plans.description: If the checking rook stands too close, walk the king toward it: each check loses the rook a file until it must abandon the checks or the pawn queens.

success.note: King-to-rook distance is geometry outside this vocabulary.

plans.label: Checks from the long side
plans.description: Keep the rook checking from the long side of the pawn — with several files between rook and pawn — so the attacking king cannot approach the rook and shelter beside the pawn at the same time.

success.note: Holding is an outcome and has no structural signature here.

plans.label: King to the short side
plans.description: Put the defending king on the short side of the pawn so it does not block its own rook's checking lane on the long side.

success.note: Which side is short depends on the pawn's file and the kings — not rules arithmetic.

watch: Fires for the rook-and-pawn-versus-rook census with a passed knight- to bishop-file pawn on the seventh; whether the attacking king stands in front of the pawn and the defending king is cut off — the actual Lucena conditions — is king geometry this vocabulary cannot express. Verify on the board.
A rook pawn on the seventh is deliberately excluded from the trigger: with an a- or h-pawn the bridge often fails and the position is a different, far more drawish story.
Extra pawns are not excluded by the census; count them yourself.
Colour convention: White is authored as the stronger/attacking side. Mirror the plans when the colours are reversed; the trigger fires only for the White-side census.
typicalMistakes: Checking or shuffling with the attacker's rook instead of building the bridge — the win has a concrete four-step shape, not a squeeze.
Building the bridge on the fifth or sixth rank, where the king finds no shelter behind it.
Defending with checks from one or two files away: out of checking distance the attacking king simply walks to the rook.
Putting the defending king on the long side, where it blocks its own rook's checks.
